presentation.summary: Show downloaded YouTube channels and playlists as TV series: one season per year, one episode per video. Single videos can be movies.
presentation.description_markdown: Maps a YouTube channel (or playlist) to a series, each year with uploads to a season, and each video to an episode dated by its upload, so channels downloaded by TubeSync, yt-dlp or similar tools behave like TV shows in Silo. Titles, descriptions, durations and thumbnails come from the YouTube Data API. Episodes are numbered MMDDxx within the year, as ZeroQI's Absolute Series Scanner numbers YouTube channels for Plex. A single video kept in a movie library is a movie, found by the video ID in its file name. The provider is installed disabled so it only runs in the libraries where you enable it.
presentation.setup_markdown:
1. Create a YouTube Data API v3 key in the Google Cloud console and enter it under **YouTube** below.
2. Name each channel's folder after the channel, or put its ID in the name: `Channel Name [youtube-UCxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx]`. A playlist folder takes `[youtube-PLxxxx]`.
3. Name each file with its upload date, as TubeSync's `{yyyy_mm_dd} - {title_full} [{key}].{ext}` does: Silo links a dated file to the episode uploaded that day.
4. Keep the channels in a TV library of their own and enable **YouTube** there as the only series metadata provider, with TVDB and TMDB off: Silo prefers any candidate with a TVDB, TMDB or IMDb ID, so a TV show with a channel's name would win.
5. For single videos, make a movie library with **YouTube** as its only movie metadata provider, and name each file with the video's ID and upload year: `Title [xxxxxxxxxxx] (2024).mkv`.

capabilities.description: YouTube channels and playlists as TV series, and single videos as movies.

fields.label: API key
fields.description: A YouTube Data API v3 key. The default quota (10,000 units a day) covers listing thousands of videos a day; a channel search costs 100 units.

fields.label: Upload date time zone
fields.description: The time zone your downloader dates files in (an IANA name such as America/New_York). yt-dlp and TubeSync use UTC, the default. Videos uploaded near midnight only link when this matches.

fields.label: Seasons
fields.description: How a channel's videos are grouped. One season per year numbers episodes MMDDxx (S2024E10201); one season lists every video in season 1, numbered YYYYMMDDxx (S1E2024010201). Changing it renumbers every episode, so pick it before a channel has watch history.

fields.label: Backdrop
fields.description: The background art of a series, or of a movie (for a movie, the thumbnail is the video's own). Channel banners and video thumbnails are full of logos and lettering, which makes the description written over them hard to read; none keeps a plain background.

fields.label: List uploads from
fields.description: The first year whose uploads become episodes, for every channel and playlist. Empty lists every upload, which for a channel you follow from last year on means thousands of episodes without a file. Set it no later than the year of your oldest download: a file from an earlier year links to no episode.

fields.label: List uploads from, by channel
fields.description: A year for one channel or playlist, where it differs from the setting above: its ID, =, and the year, one to a line, such as UCuk26DMu7ewAkC-ntx7esiA=2023. Use =all for a channel you have downloaded whole.

fields.label: Episode descriptions
fields.description: How much of a video's description an episode carries. YouTube descriptions run to 5,000 characters, much of it links and hashtags, and Silo is sent every episode of a season at each scan of a folder: with one season, the whole channel. A shorter description ends at a paragraph, a line or a sentence where it can. Changing this takes effect as each channel is next refreshed.
